Huntley College of Agriculture Specialist Credential Required | Notes | Program Website Specialist Credential Required: 29 units AGS 3000 - Advocacy in Agricultural Science (2) AGS 5050 - Youth and Adult Leadership Programs (3) AGS 5430 - Program Planning and Development (3) AGS 5440 - Procedures in Agricultural Education (3) AGS 5440A - Procedures in Agricultural Education Activity (1) AGS 5441 - Early Field Experiences (3) AGS 5442 - Agriculture Skills and Facilities (3) AGS 5442A - Agriculture Skills and Facilities Activity (1) AGS 5450 - Field Practices and Supervision (4) AGS 5450A - Field Practices and Supervision Activity (2) AGS 5470 - Teaching Methods in Agricultural Systems Technology (3) AGS 5470L - Teaching Methods in Agriculture Systems Technology Laboratory (1) Notes: In addition to meeting subject matter competencies, as outlined by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialling, candidates for the Agriculture Specialist Credential are required to have proof of a minimum of 3000 hours or more of verified work experience in the agriculture industry. The requirements for both the Single Subject and the Agricultural Specialist Credentials may be completed concurrently. A limited number of courses may be taken at the undergraduate level. Candidates should consult with the Agricultural Specialist Credential program coordinator prior to enrolling in any courses to be used for credentialing purposes Add to My Favorites (opens a new window) Share this Page Facebook this Page (opens a new windo

courses.title: Advocacy in Agricultural Science
courses.description: Overview of agriculture programs including goals and purposes of all educational levels of education in agriculture. Course focuses on developing students’ abilities in presenting personal and researched views of the agricultural industry and developing students ability to advocate for the industry as a whole.

courses.title: Youth and Adult Leadership Programs
courses.description: Organization, history, philosophy, administration and procedures in advising of the Future Farmers Association (FFA) chapters and conducting classes for out-of-school youth and adults. Surveys and plans for development of rural and urban adult programs, FFA and Young Farmer programs, techniques and methods.

courses.title: Program Planning and Development
courses.description: Study of career opportunities in agriculture. Program development in such areas as the Future Farmers of America, and other youth groups. Supervised practice including cooperative work experience in agriculture. Development of up-to-date approaches in an integrated program. Operating policies and procedures.

courses.title: Procedures in Agricultural Education
courses.description: Approaches to the learning process and development of daily and unit plans as well as the utilization of resources. Class demonstration in teaching procedures with emphasis being given to lesson development, micro-teaching, and the development of pedagogical skills including development analysis, assessment and evaluation.

courses.title: Procedures in Agricultural Education Activity
courses.description: Approaches to the learning process and development of daily and unit plans as well as the utilization of resources. Class demonstration in teaching procedures with emphasis being given lesson development, micro-teaching, and the development of pedagogical skills including development analysis, assessment and evaluation.

courses.title: Early Field Experiences
courses.description: An overview of Agricultural Education in the public schools. Professional type experience new to the student so that a valuable contribution toward career development results. Supervised, focused observation/participation at the secondary school level. Written reports necessary.

courses.title: Agriculture Skills and Facilities
courses.description: Exploring the development, operation, and maintenance of agriculture education facilities. Skills necessary for implementing project based instruction, laboratory activities, and technology applications in agriculture education will be demonstrated. Emphasis will be on management of program, facilities, teaching skill development and community involvement.

courses.title: Agriculture Skills and Facilities Activity
courses.description: Development, operation, and maintenance of agriculture education facilities. Skills necessary for implementing project based instruction, laboratory activities, and technology applications in agriculture education will be demonstrated. Emphasis will be on management of program, facilities, teaching skill development and community involvement.

courses.title: Field Practices and Supervision
courses.description: Organization and implementation of an instructional program in agricultural education. Field application of Future Farmers of America, supervised practice, and classroom instruction.

courses.title: Field Practices and Supervision Activity
courses.description: Organization and implementation of an instructional program in agricultural education. Field application of Future Farmers of America, supervised practice, and classroom instruction.

courses.title: Teaching Methods in Agricultural Systems Technology
courses.description: Organizing agriculture mechanics operations & workshops, planning shop curriculum, determining technical course content, and instructing youth and adults in industrial settings. Student directed activities, demonstration, and presentations; evaluation of performance; analysis of skill development.

courses.title: Teaching Methods in Agriculture Systems Technology Laboratory
courses.description: Organizing agriculture mechanics operations & workshops, planning shop curriculum, determining technical course content, and instructing youth and adults in industrial settings. Student directed activities, demonstration, and presentations; evaluation of performance; analysis of skill development.
